newsitem.title: MEXICO: Seven dead, 54 hurt in Mexican prison riot.
newsitem.headline: Seven dead, 54 hurt in Mexican prison riot.

text.p: Seven inmates were killed and 55 others injured on Monday during a battle with guns and Molotov cocktails between rival prison gangs in the southern Mexican city of Oaxaca, authorities said.
The riot raged for most of the day before authorities were able to regain control of the Santa Maria Ixcotel prison late on Monday, the Oaxaca state government said in a statement.
Televisa television network showed bloodied prisoners, both dead and alive, piled outside the hospital gates. Some of the wounded groaned in pain.

"The dead were mostly smashed on the head with iron bars, wooden clubs, rocks. There was glass everywhere. They threw Molotov cocktails down the corridors and there were blood stains on the wall," Benjamin Soriano, spokesman for the local Mexican League for the Defence of Human Rights, told Reuters.
Soriana was allowed to visit the jail on Monday as part of a human rights delegation, but prison guards and riot police were forced to remain outside.

He said the clash erupted when rival gangs fought for the right to represent the prison population on a so-called "board of directors." He said inmates told him prison officials had given one side weapons, including pistols and a machine gun.
More than six hours after the riot erupted, state government said it had confirmed six deaths and 55 people injured.
Soriano said a group of Indian peasants arrested last year and held in the jail on charges of belonging to the rebel Popular Revolutionary Army were not involved in the uprising.
